0.name: Parks Inspection Program — Inspections
0.note: The only proxy that measures the park itself. Ratings are A for acceptable and U for unacceptable, on cleanliness and overall_condition. 151,484 inspections in total, about 6,500 each year, so filter the year on the server. PIP inspects a ZONE and names it B007-01; cut the suffix to reach the parent property B007.

1.name: DPR Parks Properties
1.note: 2,059 sites with shapes. FacDB carries no prop_id, so the proxy reaches a geography on its own, the same way the schools case uses the DOE point file. After the zone rollup, 1,428 of 2,406 PIP sites match a shape (59.4%), and those carry 83.1% of all inspections. Of the 978 misses, 974 use a non-standard id (BT## tree districts, BR borough-wide, _temp) and are not discrete parks; only 4 are true property ids.

2.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table S1901 — median household income by census tract
2.note: An area proxy. It describes the households around a park, not the park. Only the census-tract layer carries a true median.

3.name: NYPD complaints, year to date 2026, pulled 2026-06-29
3.note: An area proxy. Crime is point data, so every layer gets a true value.

4.name: DPR Parks Properties — acquisition date
4.note: The vintage of a park. A park is land, not a building, thus it carries no construction year: only 33% of the park units hold a BIN at all, and that BIN is a comfort station or a recreation building. The acquisition date is the year the land became a park. 1,972 of 2,059 properties carry one, and the units reach 93.6% through the same spatial join that PIP uses. WARNING: acquisition is not construction — a park acquired in 1936 can hold a playground of 2015. WARNING: a year is not oriented.
